text: So the true test is does it run on my LinkedIn?
brief: The question of the whole episode. Set up 'the test': Claude on one side, Henry's LinkedIn on the other, and a connection that has not been proven yet. e.g. a Claude spark tile and a LinkedIn 'in' tile drawn as paper cutouts; a dashed wire draws between them on 'run'; a big hand-drawn question mark / test-tube or 'TEST' label pops on 'true test'; on 'LinkedIn' the LinkedIn tile pops. Feels like the opening of an experiment.

text: People have told me that I have a ghostwriter on LinkedIn. Honestly, it's just AI.
brief: Rumour → reveal. On 'People have told me' comment bubbles pop in around (e.g. 'who writes these?', 'you have a ghostwriter?'). On 'ghostwriter' a cute paper ghost appears typing at a tiny desk/laptop. On 'Honestly, it's just AI' the ghost's sheet is whisked off revealing the Claude spark/AI underneath, bubbles get crossed out or a stamp lands. Tasteful, witty, not cartoon-busy.

text: I ran a challenge in May and I posted 30 days straight, no fail, Monday to Friday.
brief: The May challenge as a calendar. Real data: window Mon 4 May → Tue 2 Jun 2026, he posted every weekday (Mon–Fri) = 22 posting days; weekends greyed. On 'challenge in May' a paper calendar card flips in titled MAY CHALLENGE; as he says 'posted 30 days straight' ticks sweep across the weekday cells in order with a running day counter; on 'no fail' a streak/flame or '0 missed' mark lands; on 'Monday to Friday' the M–F column headers get the orange underline. This beat is the one Henry called static: make it feel alive and satisfying.

text: So 36 posts in 30 days, Claude wrote them. Buffer is the app that I'm using, posted them.
brief: Who did what. On '36 posts' a counter rolls up to 36 while mini post cards stack/fan. On 'Claude wrote them' a Claude box writes lines into a card (pen/scribble). On 'Buffer is the app that I'm using, posted them' the cards travel through a Buffer box (queue/stack icon) and land on LinkedIn. Clear left-to-right pipeline: Claude (writes) → Buffer (posts) → LinkedIn.

text: So how it went? 9,600 impressions, a median of 134 per post against 217 for the rest of my year. More posts didn't mean it reached more people.
brief: The results, honestly. 'So how it went?' → a results card opens. '9,600 impressions' → an eye/impressions counter rolls to 9,600. 'a median of 134 per post against 217 for the rest of my year' → two bars grow: 'May challenge' 134 (accent) vs 'rest of year' 217 (ink, taller), numbers counting with the bars. 'More posts didn't mean it reached more people' → a small chart: posts line climbs while reach line stays flat, ending with a hand-written 'more posts ≠ more reach'. Two or three clean sub-scenes inside one MG with quick transitions.

text: What it helped me to do is directly on my LinkedIn, it actually does help me do the posting when I put one video, one photo and a poster inside.
brief: The money shot: Claude does the posting. A Claude chat window (paper UI mock). On 'one video', 'one photo', 'a poster' three file cards drop into the chat input exactly on each word (video has a play triangle, photo a mountain/sun, poster a tall card with an orange header). Before that, on 'directly on my LinkedIn' a LinkedIn tile sits at the right waiting; on 'posting' Claude sends and a LinkedIn post card (Henry Chua · now) goes live with a check/'POSTED' mark. Use the real post: poster 'The AI Driving License' + class photo thumbnails as simple shapes.

text: Claude actually checked my old project files And totally it took about 10 minutes.
brief: Speed + context. On 'checked my old project files' a stack of project folders/files fans out and a magnifier (or scanning beam) passes over them, each getting a small tick. On 'totally it took about 10 minutes' a stopwatch/clock face sweeps quickly to 10:00 with a big '10 MIN' landing on 'minutes'.

text: Now this is crazy because in the past I have to use Buffer to do it.
brief: IN THE PAST (sepia/rewind feel within the palette, e.g. ink-only, greyed paper, a 'BEFORE' tab). Show the manual Buffer routine as a slow checklist that a hand cursor ticks one by one: copy the post → open Buffer → upload media → pick a time → schedule. On 'crazy' a little exclamation; on 'Buffer to do it' the Buffer card is circled. Should feel tedious in a witty way, not ugly.

text: now with this prompt, it can be done entirely through Claude, as long as you have the right measures to connect to LinkedIn.
brief: NOW. A single prompt bar types (e.g. 'post this to my LinkedIn') on 'with this prompt'. On 'entirely through Claude' the same steps from the past beat tick off instantly in a cascade inside Claude. On 'right measures to connect to LinkedIn' a plug/connector snaps into the LinkedIn tile with a small lock and a label 'via Buffer API · LinkedIn-approved' (this is the honest mechanism). Contrast with B08: fast, clean, accent colour.

text: So always please check for your third-party apps if it's LinkedIn verified
brief: Safety check. An app-permission card list: 'Buffer' with a LinkedIn-verified shield ✓, and a sketchy unnamed 'auto-poster' with a ✗. A magnifier checks them on 'check your third-party apps'; on 'LinkedIn verified' a big verified shield/badge stamps down. Don't name any real bad app.

text: If you just started and don't really know what to do, use Buffer. Only use Claude to do this if you're experienced and you're comfortable with it.
brief: Who should use what. A fork / two paths from 'YOU': 'Just started? → Buffer' (on 'just started' … 'use Buffer') and 'Experienced & comfortable? → Claude' (on 'experienced'). Make it save-worthy: it ends as a clean two-row summary card (Beginner → Buffer · free plan | Experienced → Claude + one prompt). Honest footnote small: 'Claude posts through Buffer's API'.

text: comment GHOST and I'll send you my workflow.
brief: CTA, only 62 frames (2 s), smaller canvas 820x420 placed at 130/236 above Henry's big card. Words available: 'comment GHOST and I'll send you my workflow' (the 'If you like what you see' part is before this MG starts). An Instagram-style comment field types 'GHOST' fast and sends, then a DM bubble slides in with a 'my workflow' file card. Big, readable, punchy; 'GHOST' must be the biggest word.
